Subject: Post-demo: Data retention & deletion SLAs (next steps)

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning, Alex — great conversation. As promised, summary and next steps around data retention and deletion SLAs so your security and contracting teams can review.

Summary of what we covered:
- Redwood supports configurable retention policies at the tenant and route level; default is 90 days for request logs and 7 days for full request bodies unless configured otherwise.
- Deletion: we support on-request deletion with a 30-day completion SLA for primary data; backups are purged on a 90-day schedule after deletion is requested (see details below).
- Logs/backups: we retain operational logs separately for 1 year by default; we can scope log retention to exclude request bodies to reduce exposure.
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II compliant; I can share the report under an NDA.

Next steps (owners):
1) Share SOC 2 report and retention SLA table with Amaya security (Marissa) — attached.
2) Rishi to confirm whether backups are encrypted at rest and the exact backup purge cadence.
3) Neha to provide clarification on log retention and options to redact request bodies from logs.
4) Alex to loop in Contracts for any SLA language edits.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_v2025.pdf (redacted) and Data_Retention_SLA_Table.xlsx

If you want, we can also schedule a short follow-up with your security lead to walk through the SOC 2 artifacts.

Alex — quick answers inline to keep the thread tidy.

> 2) Deletion SLA: when you say 30 days for primary data, does that include all derived artifacts (embeddings, index shards)?
We treat "primary request data" (raw request + response bodies) and derived artifacts (embeddings, indexes) separately. Our standard process:
- Primary data deletion request triggers immediate deletion from the active store and indexes within the 30-day SLA.
- Derived artifacts: embeddings and model-specific indexes are deleted within the same 30-day window by default, but we can offer a contractual SLA to accelerate to 14 days for enterprise customers (would need to scope by dataset size).

> 3) Backups: are backups stored in a separate account/partition? How long after deletion request are snapshots removed?
Backups are stored in an encrypted, access-controlled bucket within our cloud account. Snapshots that contain deleted data are scheduled for removal on a 90-day cycle by default. We can offer an addendum to shorten that to 30 days for regulated customers, but that requires coordination with our infra team and additional fee in some cases. All backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and access is restricted.

> 4) Logs: can request bodies be redacted immediately while preserving timing/metadata for debugging?
Yes — we support a redaction pipeline that strips request/response bodies on ingest while preserving metadata (timestamps, route IDs, latency). This can be configured in your tenant settings; by default redaction is optional.

I attached a short spreadsheet (Data_Retention_SLA_Table.xlsx) with canonical SLA windows and the optional enterprise accelerations. Happy to jump on a call with Priya to walk through specifics.

- Rishi

Hi Priya/Alex — following up with some implementation-level notes that might help your security team decide: 

- Redaction options: 1) redact at ingest (bodies never persisted), 2) redact in logs only (bodies kept in short-term store then purged), 3) full retention with targeted redaction on export. Option 1 gives the strongest privacy guarantees but reduces debugging fidelity.

- Embedding/index deletion: when you request deletion, we run a job that removes entries from vector indexes and the embedding store; for very large corpora this is done in batched jobs — time to completion depends on corpus size and we surface progress via the Console.

- Audit logs & proofs: we emit audit events for deletion requests and completion; we can provide a signed digest or export for your auditors upon request.

If helpful, I can prepare a short tech note outlining transactional guarantees and a sample deletion flow (API call -> queue -> active store deletion -> index purge -> backup snapshot marking).

Cheers,
